:::{#def-quotient}

#### Quotient

For real numbers $a$ and $b$ with $b \neq 0$,
the **quotient** of $a$ by $b$
is the result of dividing $a$ by $b$:

$$\frac{a}{b}$$

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#def-fraction}
#### Fraction

A quotient $\frac{a}{b}$ (@def-quotient) is also called a **fraction**.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#def-numerator}
#### Numerator

In a fraction $\frac{a}{b}$ (@def-fraction), $a$ is its **numerator**.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#def-denominator}
#### Denominator

In a fraction $\frac{a}{b}$ (@def-fraction), $b$ is its **denominator**.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-fraction}
#### Numerator and denominator of a fraction

The fraction $\frac{6}{4}$ has numerator $6$ and denominator $4$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-quotient}
#### A quotient

The quotient of $6$ by $4$ is $\frac{6}{4} = 1.5$.
The quotient of $6$ by $0$ is undefined,
because @def-quotient requires a nonzero denominator.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#def-follow-up}
#### Follow-up

In a study that observes participants over time,
a participant's **follow-up** is the length of time the study observes that participant.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#def-person-years}
#### Person-years

In a study that observes participants over time,
the study's **person-years** are the sum of the follow-up times (@def-follow-up) of all participants,
measured in years.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-person-years}
#### Counting person-years

If $10$ people are each followed for $2$ years,
the study has $10 \cdot 2 = 20$ person-years.
If one person is followed for $3$ years and another for $\tfrac{1}{2}$ year,
the study has $3 + \tfrac{1}{2} = 3.5$ person-years.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#def-rate}
#### Rate

A **rate** is a quotient of two quantities,
usually with a denominator that measures time,
such as weeks or person-years of follow-up (@def-person-years).
For example, $12$ new cases in $4$ weeks
is a rate of $\frac{12}{4} = 3$ new cases per week,
and $30$ cases over $10{,}000$ person-years of follow-up
is a rate of $\frac{30}{10{,}000} = 0.003$ cases per person-year.

:::

::: notes
cf. <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rate_(mathematics)>
:::
